text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer states the ride is plush, smooth and comfortable, with air suspension available on higher trims. Reviewer states the 2,335 kg car feels heavy in corners and rough B-roads unsettle it. Reviewer states the steering offers little feel. Reviewer states the cabin is very quiet. Reviewer states a cold-weather motorway test returned 3.3 mi/kWh, projecting about 290 miles, roughly 120 miles short of the official 411-mile figure. Reviewer states DC charging reaches 310 kW with 10-80% in as little as 22 minutes, though few chargers can deliver that rate. Reviewer states the 14.5-inch portrait touchscreen and 9-inch driver display are crisp, and the Google-based system is quick and easy to use. Reviewer states there are no physical climate controls; physical controls are limited to station-skip buttons and a volume controller. Reviewer states some functions are fiddly because the glovebox release and mirror adjustment run through the touchscreen, and the menus are fiddly to set up. Reviewer praises the materials and fit and finish of the cabin. Reviewer states one test car had a minor clunk from a front seat. Reviewer states the front seats are well supported and comfortable. Reviewer states the high rear floor leaves rear passengers' legs raised with little under-thigh support, and rear headroom is only just adequate under the sloping roof. Reviewer flags poor rear visibility as a recurring criticism. Reviewer states the driver assistance and safety systems are comprehensive, well integrated and unobtrusive. Reviewer rates the audio systems as excellent, with Bowers & Wilkins fitted on Ultra. Reviewer states all models are well equipped and even the Plus trim feels like a well-appointed luxury car. Reviewer's dimensions comparison shows the boot at 424 litres against 490 litres for the BMW i5. Reviewer criticises the short standard warranty of three years or 60,000 miles.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer states the straight-line pace is addictive, especially for motorway overtakes. Reviewer states the car charges at up to 250 kW, about 30 minutes 10-80% on a V3 Supercharger. Reviewer states the Plaid corners flat but the steering lacks feel in every mode. Reviewer states the Plaid's seats are not very supportive, so occupants get thrown around on twisty roads. Reviewer states the indicator switches on the steering wheel do not help the user experience. Reviewer states build quality has improved, with most touched surfaces worthy of a roughly GBP 100,000 car. Reviewer states some external panel gaps are still large. Reviewer notes there is no Apple CarPlay or Android Auto. Reviewer states the gear stalk is gone and almost everything, including lights and wipers, runs through the touchscreen, with wipers buried in menus. Reviewer calls Autopilot one of the smoothest and most advanced systems of its type, though the name is misleading and the driver must stay attentive. Reviewer highlights the 709-litre boot (1,739 litres with seats folded). Reviewer states the car is sold only in left-hand drive in the UK, which causes practical problems such as paying at car park machines. Reviewer names the BMW i7 as a rival luxury limousine that is quieter than the Model S.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer states all versions are very quick, with precise accelerator response for smooth driving. Reviewer states the car is among the quietest EVs at motorway speeds. Reviewer states the Model 3 is less engaging to drive than the BMW i4. Reviewer states the steering lacks feedback. Reviewer states the suspension is firm with some patter at low speeds, though not uncomfortable. Reviewer states efficiency is class-leading, 4.4 mi/kWh in the RWD test. Reviewer highlights Supercharger access with favourable tariffs and straightforward billing. Reviewer praises the large, responsive 15.4-inch touchscreen with fast processing. Reviewer states the sat-nav plots charging stops en route and preconditions the battery. Reviewer states the lack of physical buttons hurts usability; the hazard switch sits by the mirror and the glovebox opens only via screen or voice. Reviewer states the cabin does not feel as solid or expensive as the BMW i4 or Mercedes CLA, despite improved fit and finish since the 2024 facelift. Reviewer lists ventilated seats among the car's strengths. Reviewer notes there is no Apple CarPlay or Android Auto. Reviewer states paying about GBP 7,000 for Full Self-Driving is not worthwhile because some features are not yet usable. Reviewer states the 594-litre boot with deep underfloor storage is big, against 470 litres for the BMW i4. Reviewer states the narrow saloon boot opening makes loading harder than in hatchbacks such as the BMW i4. Reviewer states the low rear seats give limited under-thigh support. Reviewer states even the base RWD is well equipped.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Long-term tester states the charger-finding tools in both Android Auto and the car's own system worked well, showing charger speed and free plugs during a trip to France. Long-term tester reports rapid charging gained about 150 miles in a 20-minute stop and found French rapid chargers with bank-card payment almost seamless. Long-term tester reports 3.2 mi/kWh overall, matching the official 4.0 mi/kWh only in slow 50 mph traffic, and at 80 mph range fell from about 350 to about 260 miles (WLTP 443 miles). Long-term tester found the car composed and comfortable on motorways, with a smooth ride and stable tracking, though composed rather than fun. Long-term tester found the boot very large for a family of four on holiday. Long-term tester states the parcel shelf must be detached before loading a full boot, to avoid bending it when closing the tailgate. Long-term tester states rear legroom is limited because the bench sits low, forcing taller passengers to bend their knees, and under-thigh support could be better. Long-term tester states the voice control did not understand his commands. Long-term tester reports the touch-to-open charging flaps kept opening while the car was being washed. Long-term tester praises the Malpelo Blue paint and the estate's shape. Long-term tester finds the EV-specific front, with blanked grille and a body-coloured panel between the headlights, less appealing than the petrol/hybrid A6. Long-term tester states the black plastic sill panels look cheap and pick up fingerprints.
